title: Packing Thanksgiving Leftovers

cardDescription: Sort the lids, labels, and containers used to share the food remaining after a Thanksgiving gathering.
focus: The clues describe packing and labeling, rather than prescribing storage times or temperatures.
solvingTip: Look for the container first, then its covering and label.

answerNotes.LABEL: Labels can identify contents and the date they were packed.
answerNotes.DATE: A written date identifies a day; this puzzle sets no storage-time rule.

title: Bringing a Dish to the Potluck
description: Plan a shared Thanksgiving meal through sign-up lists, covered dishes, and the people bringing them.
cardDescription: Plan a shared Thanksgiving meal through sign-up lists, covered dishes, and the people bringing them.
subtheme: Bringing a Dish to the Potluck
focus: At a potluck, guests contribute different dishes; the host may coordinate the list to avoid duplicates.
solvingTip: Separate what people bring from what the organizer writes down.

List used to record which guest will bring each dish

answerNotes.POTLUCK: Potluck describes how the meal is shared, rather than one specific menu.
answerNotes.SIGNUP: A sign-up can help the organizer see missing items or repeated dishes.
answerNotes.CARRIER: A carrier holds the dish during transport; it is not the food itself.
answerNotes.ALLERGY: The puzzle identifies a planning word and gives no medical advice.
answerNotes.SERVING: Serving can name a portion or the act of offering food.

description: Follow a holiday rail visit from a reserved ticket to the reunion waiting at the station.
cardDescription: Follow a holiday rail visit from a reserved ticket to the reunion waiting at the station.
focus: Travel clues focus on the passenger journey and meeting arrangements, rather than locomotive machinery.

answerNotes.REUNION: A reunion describes the gathering, not the journey used to reach it.
answerNotes.PLATFORM: A platform is on the station side, separate from the rail car.
answerNotes.RESERVE: Some services assign seats; others reserve travel without a numbered seat.
answerNotes.LUGGAGE: Luggage is a collective word; a suitcase is one individual item.
answerNotes.ARRIVAL: Arrival contrasts with departure, when a journey begins.

cardDescription: Remember a shared holiday dish through handwritten quantities, recipe boxes, and notes from earlier cooks.
focus: A recipe card records both ingredients and method; an added note may preserve a family variation.

answerNotes.MEASURE: Measuring identifies quantity before ingredients are combined.
answerNotes.SERVINGS: Servings describe a recipe's yield rather than its cooking time.
answerNotes.MARGIN: Margin notes can preserve changes without replacing the original directions.

cardDescription: Step outside after the holiday meal for a small neighborhood scene of bare branches, fading light, and conversation.
focus: This is an observational walk, with familiar words for surroundings and company rather than fitness targets.
solvingTip: Use the location or sense described: something seen, heard, or walked along.

Time when daylight is fading toward night

answerNotes.SIDEWALK: A sidewalk is beside the road, while a crosswalk goes across it.
answerNotes.DUSK: Dusk refers to the light after sunset rather than a fixed clock time.

answerNotes.CHAT: Chat describes informal talk rather than a formal speech.
answerNotes.PORCH: A porch adjoins a building; it is different from a public sidewalk.
